notes.text: Test Day - includes the year as the first two digits followed by the 3-digit day of the year (where any late-hour transition to the next day is neglected). MFC - identifies the maximum flow rate of the specified ACME Mass Flow Controller (MFC) in slpm on a nitrogen basis. Fuel conc. - (as diluted with nitrogen on a volume basis) was varied between tests and sometimes during tests where the listing here accounts for both. However, it does not account for extinction that sometimes occurred before the flame fully reached the lowest concentration. Flames ignited is the number ignited on that test day.

decisions: One row is one test day (row_kind test_day).

The 'Fuel Bottle' column carries a spreadsheet fill series (40% CH4, 40% CH5, ... 40% CH14; 100% C2H4 ... 100% C2H11): the formula in that cell is not trusted. The fuel is taken from 'Test Type' when it names one ('Methane based test', 'Ethylene based test'); for 'Improved coflow tests' it is taken from the bottle cell only when the formula is CH4 or C2H4, else null. fuel_raw keeps the bottle cell as written.
'Test Day' is YYDDD (table note): turned into a date.
No oxygen, pressure or flow-speed column: those fields are null.

notes.text: Note 1 Derived from measured CO2 production and referenced to initial O2 concentration reported by ISS.
Note 2 The PMMA portion was completely consumed but the Nomex was not ignited.
Note 3 This is the length of fuel with significant visible damage.
Note 4 The flames remain anchored at the base of the sample which has a very slow regression rate (0.01 to 0.04 mm/s)

decisions: The table has the microgravity result and the normal-gravity (1-g) result side by side: they are four separate outcomes, each tagged with its gravity. The test's own gravity stays the investigation's (microgravity).

The two microgravity headers start with '?' in the saved file ('?-g Burn Length'); they sit beside the '1-g' columns and are read as the low-gravity ones. The second is titled 'Spread Length' but its cells are rates in mm/s: stored as a spread rate.
Cells carry their unit ('20 cm/s', '2.1 mm/s', '29 cm'); text results ('Complete', 'Acceleratory', 'Insignificant', 'n/a', 'Note 4') are null with raw kept. '~ 0' is read as 0.

Samples 2-6 and 2-9 have an empty Material cell (it looks like a merged cell under the one above): fuel stays null and 'fuel_from_row_above' shows what the cell above reads, as a hint that is not asserted.
Thickness cells '037 mm' and 'See Fig. 5' go into fuel_size as written.
Rows for flow visualization data and the four note rows are skipped; the notes are kept as table notes.
